fix: Nostr profile actions fail for paired dashboard operators (#145932)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where paired dashboard operators could not save or import a Nostr profile when their browser held only its device credential. Save & Publish and Import from Relays each returned HTTP 401, then displayed `e?.trim is not a function`.

The dashboard handoff in `docs/web/control-ui/connect-and-pair.md`, paired-operator Control UI read authorization, and profile editor in `docs/channels/nostr.md` establish this contract. The defect was reproduced on pinned main `3b88500581f6e9bf28f4e6ef91f2deb5483c16c7` through the real browser and Gateway.

Related: #138975 preserves recovery when a second credential exists; this fixes the device-only case. #105781 concerns import cancellation and drafts and remains separate. Related #78712 discusses shared-secret trusted-operator defaults; this repair preserves that shipped policy. Found by the adversarial round; no external reporter.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared HTTP authorization owner now verifies current paired-operator credentials for plugin routes and passes their verified scopes to the existing runtime scope owner. Nostr keeps its admin requirement. Request headers cannot expand a device grant; ordinary plugin routes retain their write ceiling.

The existing plugin request scope also carries a Gateway-owned `revalidate` callback. Nostr, Admin HTTP RPC, Beam, and Geolocation call it after input reading/validation and before starting effects; Nostr checks after the publish queue wait and again before saving a published or imported profile. It verifies the original device grant through the same credential checker, writes the standard Gateway 401 on rejection, and stops the handler. There is no new registration option, config key, or contract version. This checkpoint does not cancel external work already in progress.

The shared Control UI JSON response boundary checks parsed objects, decodes Gateway error envelopes once, and supplies message plus HTTP status. The import adapter narrows profile text fields while preserving null values and extra fields. Channels and Browser Download use that result. Nostr-local error decoding and string-typed error assumptions are removed; profile validation details remain visible.

The decision "whether a shared or paired-device credential authenticates an operator HTTP request" is made by exactly one mechanism at `src/gateway/http-auth-utils.ts:241` (`checkHttpOperatorCredentials`).

The decision "whether an admitted device grant remains valid before handler effects" is made by exactly one mechanism at `src/gateway/http-auth-utils.ts:241` (`checkHttpOperatorCredentials`), shared by admission and the Gateway-owned request-scope callback.

The decision "how a Gateway JSON error becomes UI text with HTTP status" is made by exactly one mechanism at `ui/src/app/control-ui-auth.ts:6` (`readControlUiJsonResponse`).

## User Impact

Paired operators can publish and import their Nostr profile with their existing device session. Rejected credentials show `HTTP 401: Unauthorized`. Configured-token recovery remains available. No schema, migration implementation, config key, dependency, or protocol version changes are included.

## Invalidation

Each HTTP request rereads pairing state and verifies the current token, scopes, revocation, and issuer generation. The verifier checks the entire observed scope grant, so narrowing between lookup and verification cannot authorize the broader snapshot. Each effect checkpoint retains the original bearer and required scopes, reads current Gateway auth, and requires fresh device verification; a different successful auth method cannot replace the admitted device grant. The capability expires when its HTTP response closes. No credential cache is introduced. External operations already started are not cancelled by this checkpoint.

Real requests confirmed rotation and revocation take effect, forged admin headers fail, auth-generation changes reject old tokens, rate locks expire, and cross-origin/site mutations remain denied. The exact lookup-to-verification race is source-reviewed rather than forced by a runtime failpoint.

Each UI operation captures its connection/form/tab ownership and resolves current credentials. Existing cancellation, deadline, and generation checks suppress stale completion. The shared decoder has no cache; body decoding preserves aborts. Named-role policy and auth-bypass cache lifecycle are unchanged.

## Contention

Existing per-client credential serialization groups shared/device verification and failure accounting into one terminal attempt. No new queue or transaction is introduced. Eight concurrent invalid plugin requests under a three-failure limit yielded three 401 and five 429 responses. A valid device worked while only the shared-secret bucket was locked, was denied during the device lock, and worked after expiry. No limiter bypass or deadline reset was added. The new awaited checkpoint was exercised with body-pending revocation in real Nostr and Beam requests; neither blocked the independent public revoke command, and both rejected before their effect. Save now revalidates inside the existing queued callback, after the prior publication settles, and again before its later config write. The check cannot undo a relay publication already sent. Final packaged evidence confirms queued revocation prevents a second publication/config mutation and revocation during relay acknowledgement prevents the later config write. Public device revocation completed while requests waited; normal first publication completed successfully. No queue, relay timeout, or locking policy changed.

fix(config): preserve concurrent settings after Control UI autosave (#145939)

Related: #145660

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users changing Advanced settings could delete a concurrent file edit when a second autosave followed the first save's acknowledgement. In the reproduced case, an external French locale setting vanished even though both saves succeeded.

The documented contract allows direct config-file edits, and `ui/AGENTS.md` requires the UI to reconcile authoritative Gateway results while retaining newer user edits. The adversarial round found this follow-up to #145660.

## Why This Change Was Made

The UI now adopts the acknowledgement's canonical config and revision together, then replays only form edits made while that request was pending. Teardown uses the same replay. An unchanged successful save adopts the canonical document directly, without parsing submitted text. Newer raw text keeps its exact bytes and existing draft base, so a later stale submission still conflicts. Changed objects that become redacted values retain their explicit edits.

The decision **what configuration belongs to an acknowledged revision** is made by exactly one mechanism at `src/config/mutate.ts:1202-1220`: the server's canonical reread. The UI's reconstruction from submitted text is removed. `config.set` and `config.apply` consume one acknowledgement type; `config.patch` already consumes the canonical pair and keeps its intentional no-op contract.

No schema, migration, config key, protocol shape, version, or update behavior changes. The server contract already ships with #145660. Three production files change; the wider test diff replaces obsolete hash-only receipts in existing consumers and covers the regression.

## User Impact

A logging autosave preserves an unrelated concurrent setting. In-flight form changes, reversions, deletions, and the final save during teardown retain user intent. Stale drafts remain rejected instead of silently overwriting another writer.

## What Problem This Solves

A subscription can remain blocked for days after its provider usage view reports restored capacity. The next ordinary chat, scheduled run, or inherited agent turn keeps rejecting the same valid account. The stored provider reset deadline remains unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reconcile stored subscription blocks through the existing auth usage owner before runtime admission. After five minutes, the next demand waits for a fresh usage observation. Both persisted quota sources can recover. Additional quota buckets, workspace limits, spending controls, malformed responses, and account failures cannot falsely clear the block.

Concurrent demands share one probe per physical credential owner. The apply transaction verifies the current credential and unchanged failure generation. Each waiting caller then reads its current persisted credential and usage. Direct side questions use the same owner before preparing auth. The isolated-completion correction moves host auth through common simple-completion preparation, which awaits quota reconciliation before route selection and the immutable auth plan. The native-auth branch retains the same quota owner. Caller authority is checked again after the wait.

A fresh available usage response received during another model's ordinary failure uses that same quota transition immediately. It clears the old quota restriction before accounting for the new ordinary failure. Delayed usage responses cannot overwrite a newer quota observation, credential replacement, or successful use.

Successful use records its health observation in the existing `lastProbeAt` field. This also protects inherited accounts, whose successful turns intentionally preserve account-selection history.

Generic rate-limit accounting no longer adds a second retry cooldown after the provider quota owner has recorded that failure. Existing rows with both restrictions can reach the quota check; a fresh result retires only a rate-limit cooldown whose model scope is covered by the quota block. Authentication, disabled-account, and unrelated model cooldowns remain effective.

Operational SQLite write failures during quota reconciliation retain the stored block and allow a healthy configured fallback. The shared pending probe handles only native READONLY, IOERR, and FULL errors. The normal store writer records the error; each caller must still reload current credentials and state before admission. Constraint and other unexpected errors remain fatal.

Token renewal remains with the existing credential owner. No configuration option, schema, migration, provider plugin, or public SDK contract changes.

The current combined production diff is net-negative: 449 added lines and 467 removed lines across eight production files, a reduction of 18 lines. Tests and support are counted separately. Current signed head is `625c2c137262c475e1bec74e2ede9287672116f0`, tree `b4de089eecac78ff5468bd3dbd63e91f9768ef2f`. Product source is byte-identical to the successful correction proof at `b6ec779939db15a7ffd56aba4bb539d1ea9a2f7d`; the later test/CI follow-up passed its own affected checks. Signature and source bindings are verified; fresh exact-head integration checks remain required.

This changes the background-only admission choice introduced in #108683 (`a5d1d9e473babae7ebcb4a48c958ec5158bc9e2e`): the current demand now waits for the bounded usage check and can use restored capacity immediately. @steipete, for awareness.

## User Impact

After the five-minute recheck interval, the next ordinary turn can use the same account when upstream capacity is restored. Users do not need to restart, delete state, or sign in again to clear a stale quota block.

## Contention

The existing auth store transaction claims an admission probe and later applies its result. The network request runs between those transactions. Credential saves, other failure accounting, success updates, ordering, and shared snapshot publication use the same store owner. Success clears health and records `lastProbeAt` in that same transaction; the embedded success wrapper retains its existing asynchronous bookkeeping contract. The in-flight map coalesces admission probes by physical owner and profile within one process; failure-triggered usage probes remain separate requests and rely on the generation check when applying available or exhausted observations. Persisted claims throttle later probes across processes, but only callers in the same process share the pending result. Independent Gateway proof observed one held restored-usage request shared by main, a spawned child, and a registered cron run; all three subsequently succeeded. `health`, `cron.status`, and `models.list` completed while the request was held.

For personal accounts, the owner-directory resolver returns no agent directory. The in-flight key uses the shared path prefix plus the unique personal profile ID, so agents using the same personal account share its pending admission probe. Writes still route through the personal-account transaction, and each effective store materializes only the selected account. This source inspection does not add personal-login runtime proof.

## Invalidation

- Fresh usage or a bounded demand retry replaces or clears quota facts only through the quota owner.
- The provider's recorded reset time still expires through the existing synchronous state owner.
- Successful login, token renewal, credential replacement, account deletion, and a newly local inherited credential use the existing credential/store publication owners; waiting callers reread the current effective store.
- A newer failure generation or credential change prevents the old probe from applying.
- A committed successful use or quota probe updates `lastProbeAt`, which participates in generation matching even when no quota block existed before the request. Independent main and genuine-child overlaps verified that a delayed exhausted response cannot recreate a block after newer successful use. Inherited success preserves selection history.
- Restart reconstructs quota state from existing storage. Configuration and policy reload retain existing snapshot ownership; no separate quota cache or new persisted state is introduced.

- Saved-only clearing is observed separately from natural expiry, successful inference, and login/logout. A separate process removes only the selected profile's five persisted block fields, preserving credentials, configuration, and all other usage fields. ## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running `openclaw doctor --lint --all` after successful Skill Workshop relocation see correctly placed default-agent proposals reported as external, with another suggestion to run Doctor.

## Why This Change Was Made

Full lint reads private SQLite state while persisted skill paths still refer to the original filesystem. The existing Workshop inspection owner now receives both environments and carries them through the existing cron selector, including a persisted custom store path.

The decision `which environment a lint inspection resolves Workshop targets against` is made by exactly one mechanism at `src/commands/doctor-skill-workshop-sqlite.ts:95`: filesystem classification uses `env`, and snapshot reads use `stateEnv`. The registered check supplies the original and private environments. No post-filter or second selector is added.

## User Impact

Full lint accepts correctly relocated skills in default and explicitly configured agent directories. Genuine external targets, retained backup warnings, and stale automation references remain visible. Existing direct inspection and cron callers retain their behavior.

Related: #140948.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users selecting a model through WeChat receive no reply and a prepared-catalog configuration error when browser or meeting-plugin enablement is left at its default. Explicitly writing those defaults made the same command work.

## Why This Change Was Made

Gateway startup and reload already derive plugin activation from the authored configuration and publish the effective runtime configuration. A second request-time auto-enable pass treated materialized plugin settings as authored input and added four `enabled: true` properties that the published model owner did not contain.

Remove that second resolver and its cache. Channel starts, pairing, status, conversations, outbound selection, and queued-delivery authority checks now consume the published runtime configuration. Exact catalog matching and scoped message-action configuration selection remain intact.

The decision about effective plugin activation is made by the source-owned Gateway lifecycle at `src/gateway/server-startup-bootstrap.ts`; request consumers use its publication. This removes 60 production lines overall. It retires the request-time cache introduced in ca7b6be7cf41b9dc3721977c1e6cb7e104c9a687 after lifecycle publication became authoritative; @steipete is tagged for awareness of that removal. No config key, schema, migration, protocol, or public SDK surface changes.

This is separate from #144600, which preserves runtime defaults while applying the startup auto-enable delta. It does not remove the post-publication resolver repaired here.

## User Impact

Model commands work without hand-writing plugin defaults. Explicit disabled settings, deny rules, allowlists, and source-configured channel activation keep their existing owners.

## Evidence

- Baseline `37fa5cb7470db50a12a5f12edf46fb7ac8b3e63a`: built Gateway CLI and the external WeChat plugin's registered polling/dispatch path, using recording services. Observation-only diagnostics show exactly four requested-only enable flags and otherwise matching configurations.

- Candidate: omitted, browser-only omitted, meeting-only omitted, explicit true, and explicit false configurations all complete startup, registered model selection, a selected-model turn, config reload, and restart. Recording-provider requests follow `model-a → model-b → model-b → model-b`; omitted flags stay absent from the saved configuration.
- Real Telegram Test Server: an ordinary reply and `/models` both succeed with channel and plugin enablement omitted, exercising source-owned auto-enable.
- Real Gateway startup corpus: all 16 valid sanitized fixtures reach ready and shut down cleanly. The malformed legacy API fixture rejects as expected. Credentials are synthetic; external transports and schedulers are suppressed for this startup-only corpus check.
- New registered `channels.status` regression: baseline has one intended failure for omitted flags and two passing explicit controls. Candidate targeted validation passes **187 tests in five suites**: status, start, pairing, send, and the conversations sibling.

fix(logging): preserve pinned redaction and public URL boundaries (#145810)

## What Problem This Solves

Operators who copied the shipped redaction strings into `logging.redactPatterns` lost form-body and structured authorization protection after #145553. Public SDK and subsystem-console output could expose encoded form values and Digest credentials.

The built-in AWS secret access key detector also shortened public URL paths ending in `@latest` or followed by a query containing `@`. Compact serialized URLs could share the wrong authority state. The final file-log `message` was affected too. Ordinary 40-character hashes unnecessarily triggered a full pattern scan.

Follow-up to #145553 and #144059. Found by adversarial round 3.

## Why This Change Was Made

- `redactPatterns` replaces the string list; built-in structural protections always apply. Form-body and structured-auth preprocessing run at the owner without list-identity recognition. Every enabled resolution includes the same AWS matcher, including current copied defaults, older lists, default-plus-extra and custom-only configurations.
- `matchAwsSecretAccessKeys` owns unlabelled AWS candidate classification. Its shared value expression also supplies the fast admission check. Explicit secret-field names retain their separate field contract.
- Each candidate captures its own URL context. The scanner waits until whitespace or end to classify pending candidates, so later raw-userinfo punctuation can settle the original authority without a sibling URL overwriting it.
- Authority ends at `/`, `?`, or `#`. An `@` in a path or query cannot turn an earlier public path into userinfo. The public preservation boundary and the URL context lifetime are separate: punctuation can shorten the former, while the matching original delimiter at the same escape depth ends the latter. Query/fragment context prevents nested URL-looking text from restarting public shielding.
- Support exports replace their separate AWS regex with the shared matcher. Their vendor pass uses the existing full-context option, so long tokens and boundary assertions remain intact before support applies its full AWS marker. Existing field and private-data stages follow.

The built-in decision whether an unlabelled 40-character value is an AWS secret access key is made by exactly one mechanism at `src/logging/redact-patterns.ts:99` (`matchAwsSecretAccessKeys`). The prefilter consumes that matcher’s value probe, and diagnostic support consumes that matcher’s decisions.

## User Impact

- Built-in redaction preserves public `path@latest` and query-at paths, plus compact and escaped URL siblings. Existing raw-userinfo and nested-query credential cases remain masked.
- File logging preserves complete public URLs in the final written message. Ordinary hash-filled objects avoid the full redaction walk.
- A late review exposed slash-containing database passwords skipped by the narrowed prefilter. Baseline SDK/console masked them; the candidate leaked them. The generic URL admission probe now includes those passwords, so the existing database rule runs. AWS classification and the hash probe are unchanged.
- The established malformed numeric-port/path candidate ending in `@` still masks. Its sibling without terminal `@` stays intact. This explicit ambiguity does not redefine ordinary path `@` as authority.
- Copied string lists and custom-only lists retain form, structured-auth and bare-AWS protection in SDK and console output. `getDefaultRedactPatterns` returns only serializable strings; the internal executable registry still serves browser/default consumers. Tool and final file routes also retain their fixed string rules.
- Older copied regexes retain their literal behavior, including their previous URL false positives. Operator patterns are not rewritten, and previously damaged stored text cannot be recovered.

Support vendor rules had also lost full-context metadata. With custom-only strings, the real `gateway diagnostics export` path (`register.ts` → exporter → configured reader) stored a raw long-token tail. Actual ZIP field lengths: original11, intermediate240(red), final11(green). The custom marker masks on every pin. Default-config CLI masks upstream on all pins; injected-reader ZIP probes remain supplemental.

Configuration remains a string list. No schema, migration, protocol, CLI option, public SDK argument, or updater change is introduced. The retired custom-only form-disablement expectation was the bug; docs, SDK guidance and configuration help now describe the accepted structural contract.

## What Problem This Solves

Signal lists `Work Phone` as `work-phone` but misses its authored number/endpoint. Fresh startup reports unconfigured and never contacts that endpoint until Doctor renames the key. Runtime must work without the #138982 cleanup.

## Why This Change Was Made

The decision 'which stored key serves Signal account id X' is made by exactly one mechanism at `src/routing/account-lookup.ts:94`.

Signal declares its rule once in manifest metadata: exact keys win; normalized aliases use authored settings only with a nonempty own number. The task owner accepted own-number transport/settings, whole-root inheritance for aliases without a number, exact collision winners, and Doctor refusing cleanup that activates ignored settings.

Setup preserves restrictions in the canonical default row, even when empty, and restores its number to root. Promotion targets the runtime winner. The second correction removes command singleton/writer raw-key bypasses: selector-owned optional creation; existing selection for delete/clear. Global owner authority stays separate.

fix(backup): preserve symbolic links to external targets (#141925)

Closes #141923

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `openclaw backup create` publishes nothing when included state contains an absolute symbolic link to an external file or directory, including a dangling target.

This reworks @adele-with-a-b's reproduction and contribution under the maintainer's explicit recovery policy: preserve links and their targets, report external targets durably, and recreate the links during restore.

## Why This Change Was Made

One archive-entry policy preserves the original link target and classifies whether it names content outside the state directory, even when another declared asset includes the target. The existing traversal records external links. The manifest is sealed after that traversal and includes `externalSymbolicLinks`; no link target is followed to copy content.

The decision `how a symbolic link is recorded and whether its target is external` is made by exactly one mechanism at `src/infra/backup-archive-path-policy.ts:54`.

Restore extracts payload files and creates every link parent directory before creating the verified links. Archive path normalization preserves filename whitespace. Verification rejects entries beneath a symbolic link and checks that external-link records match the archive. Writer and reader share the existing 1 MiB manifest limit; oversized metadata fails before publication.

This intentionally reverses the absolute/escaping-target rejection from #123672 (`8c7e86a2ead`) and the owned-absolute rewrite from #136343 (`0aa9ae9f3e3`). @steipete @vsumner: the maintainer-directed recovery policy now preserves the original target text.

## User Impact

Backups complete with ordinary absolute, relative, and dangling links. The manifest, create summary, JSON output, and restore warnings identify outside-state targets. Creation never copies content through a link; a separately declared config, credentials, or workspace asset can still include that content. Absolute links still name their original locations after restore; review those paths before activating a relocated backup.

No database schema, migration, config key, CLI flag, or manifest version changes. No installation/update behavior change is claimed. Existing managed-root exclusions and SQLite snapshot/sanitization owners remain in place.

Compatibility findings: v2026.9.4 rejects preserved absolute or escaping targets. Such archives require the updated reader. Older portable relative archive links remain supported, including Windows links between drives. Absolute owned links are no longer rewritten for relocation, as required by literal target preservation. The manifest now appears after the payload and always includes an external-link report, which can be empty. Readers retain the older portable-relative archive contract when that report is absent. Old cross-asset links are still reported as outside-state during verification and restore.

fix(plugins): take a fresh lifecycle lease when a channel starts so provider login can apply settings (#145761)

## Problem

Telegram `/login xai` saves credentials, then fails with `ProviderAuthConfigApplyError: Credentials saved, but provider settings could not be applied: plugin lifecycle lease core:plugin-lifecycle/global was lost`. The provider is left half-configured. Reports also show `Unknown provider: xai` from `/models xai all`; the pinned reproduction confirms missing connection settings even when later catalog discovery succeeds.

Release blocker: affects every provider login that writes connection settings after a plugin reload on main since #145484.

## Provenance

Introduced by #145484 (`b5134de70af88e342accaba665590c7cb6b79f0b`), which is not in a release tag. The same real Telegram Test Server flow fails on that merge (exit 1) and completes on its raw parent `fde94351cacb8ef636ee3b308da920206d2a823d` (exit 0). The parent persists the subscription connection settings and completes a first turn. @steipete: this fixes the channel-lifetime handoff added with live plugin reload; it preserves that feature.

Both runs use the bundled xAI plugin and a recording HTTPS fixture for device authorization, token exchange, model discovery, and inference. The command is:

```sh
node "$PROOF/login-harness/xai/run.mjs" "$TELEGRAM_E2E_SKILL_DIR" "$OUTPUT" "$PROXY_ROOT" 21283 21289 21292 login
```

The scenario sends `/login xai`, `/models xai all`, selects an account model, and sends a turn. This proves the real channel and plugin integration with synthetic provider responses, not production account entitlement.

## Cause

Channel startup inherits the config watcher's lifecycle ownership. The channel continues after that lease closes. Its later settings writer sees the inherited context and fails the closed-lease assertion instead of acquiring current ownership.

A private diagnostic captured `closed: true`, acquisition through `startTrackedReload`, and the later assertion through `writeProviderAuthConfig`. The lease table was empty after normal release. This was not heartbeat loss.

## Fix

Clear inherited plugin lifecycle and state-file exclusion ownership at `ChannelManager.startChannel`, alongside the existing request and plugin-generation detachment. The settings writer then acquires its own lease. A genuinely closed reload lease still refuses use.

All channel starts, reload replacements, and automatic retries share this boundary. Plugin capability checks, current-registry checks, write conflict checks, and the lifecycle-lease-before-config-lock order remain intact. The runtime change uses the existing scope-exit helper. Internal option comments are shortened without changing their contracts. Production diff: +9/-40 lines.

## Regression

The new test exercises the registered config watcher and production channel restart supervisor, then writes provider settings from the restarted channel continuation. It asserts the persisted settings and independently checks that the completed reload lease refuses reuse. It adds no production test seam.

## Contention

The watcher owns the lifecycle lease while applying a reload. A restarted channel previously retained that expired ownership; now its later login competes for a fresh lease through the same owner. Config writes still acquire the lifecycle lease before the config lock. Reload serialization and per-account start/stop queues are unchanged.

Both overlap directions ran through public Gateway methods and the real Telegram login path on the repair:

- Reload during held token exchange: plugin reload succeeds in 527 ms, model-list RPC responds in 19 ms, and login plus the first turn complete.
- Login during held plugin replacement: health responds in 7.1 ms and model-list RPC in 9.7 ms. The stale replacement refuses before commit and preserves the previous runtime. After `config.get` observes the newly saved settings, one fresh `plugins.reload` succeeds in 404 ms with `restartRequired: false`. Login and the first turn complete without Gateway restart. This is refusal followed by a fresh successful reload, not first-attempt replacement success.

No retry loop or weakened lease assertion was added.

## Invalidation

Channel startup, config-triggered restart, plugin reload, and automatic channel retry all clear inherited lifecycle ownership before the new lifetime begins. Credential/config publication keeps its existing refresh owners. Gateway restart creates fresh scopes. Real closure and cancellation continue to reject the old operation.

Additional controls: bundled MiniMax chat OAuth saves settings on the repair (exit 0) and reproduces the same lease failure on baseline (exit 1). Web Models xAI sign-in passes on both baseline and repair, localizing this failure to the reloaded channel context. On the final head, the populated web picker shows options in 19.1 ms; no provider or WebSocket request starts on the click. The saved account survives fresh browser and Gateway processes.

## Known limits

Automatic appearance of a newly released model without any user action is not provided on main; tracked separately. In the retained final-head measurement, the fixture published another model at 30 seconds and `/models xai all` at 95 seconds still showed eight choices, with no subsequent catalog request.

The browser page-reload attempt hit the isolated 4 GiB cap. Fresh-browser persistence and the populated picker pass. Two native full lint attempts hit the 8 GiB cap; hosted lint is green. A supplementary root/test scan found 520 identical diagnostics on the merge tree and its main parent; all 82 diagnosed files are unchanged. These are recorded validation limits, not demonstrated regressions from this change.

CI run 34682387383, attempt 1, is **green** on this exact head and merge tree `cc9a73d7a78bed90d2d1ac1590c10689df699c90`. All four required structural checks also pass on that tree: line limits, assertion rules, unused exports, and formatting. The final merge-tree consumer census passes with no removed symbols. The earlier four-test failure did not recur in final CI and remains unexplained.

Landing requires the personal exact-head review and independent census verdict for this head. The accepted flow is sign-in → persisted settings → immediate account models → first provider turn, plus a picker that opens without a request.

fix(cli): refuse another agent's credentials after restore (#145692)

Related: #144931

## What Problem This Solves

Restoring an agent backup and registering that directory under a new agent name lets local capability inference use the original agent's saved credential. This follows supported `backup create`, `backup restore --target`, and `agents add --agent-dir` commands. Local model inference already refuses the durable owner mismatch. Follow-up to our #144931; found by the adversarial round, with no external reporter.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared local account preparation now passes the selected identity to the auth database owner before resolving credentials, including when a secrets snapshot is active. The auth reader delegates to the existing durable schema-owner assertion without requiring a newer session schema. No schema, migration, configuration, or protocol change.

The decision 'may this agent use this saved credential' is made by exactly one mechanism at `src/state/openclaw-agent-db-schema-helpers.ts:311`.

## User Impact

A restored directory registered under another name now produces the same owner-mismatch refusal across local inference commands before any provider request. Legitimate saved credentials continue to work.

## Evidence

Pinned base: `d5e652099074b5801cc7e4e3a108c035d2888e99`.

- Supported restore reproduction: base embedding exits 0 and sends one recorded provider request with the original agent's synthetic credential. The model control exits 1 with `belongs to agent ops; requested agent restored` and sends no request.
- Candidate `2e81eb5998b460c47463907b0b8fdac88b19ead0`: restored embedding and model both exit 1 with the owner mismatch and zero provider requests. All six repaired commands—embedding, image generation, image description, audio transcription, video generation, and video description—reject the foreign owner before dispatch. Model inference remains a separate unchanged control. A supplemental video-generation capture uses the configured recorder endpoint: the legitimate owner creates and downloads a video; the restored owner exits 1 with the owner mismatch and sends zero create/content requests.
- Final pre-landing rebase: head `f1a33f00c1c7cdcc332b3e5464430f46a49e044c` preserves the exact repair patch and all four changed files. The six restored-owner refusal commands and legitimate-owner video/model controls were refreshed on this head; prior pinned-base, rotation, older-state, and targeted-test evidence remains retained.
- Legitimate saved-reference accounts succeed for all six command families. The known multi-agent image-description forwarding failure remains unchanged; the sole-agent description control succeeds, as in the original proof. #145188/#145171 track that separate path.
- Rotated credentials succeed through model, embedding, image edit, describe-many, audio, video generation/download, and video description. An unavailable unrelated credential does not block the healthy account.
- Previous state: v2026.9.4 application source created a schema-19 saved account; candidate embedding succeeds with its credential through the existing schema-20 upgrade path. The older source needed only upstream build-tool repair #144831 to complete its build; application sources were unchanged from the tag.
- All six registered capability regression cases fail on the original code. Candidate capability tests: 255 passed; auth SQLite sibling: 16 passed. The helper provenance test passes after an isolation-only correction.
- A source-blind validator independently ran the supported restore and legitimate-account CLI flows on pre-rebase head `2e81eb5998b460c47463907b0b8fdac88b19ead0`: PASS. The focused post-rebase CLI refresh was run by the repair worker.
- Proof uses synthetic credentials and a loopback provider to measure actual credential routing and request absence.

## Consumers

Seven calls to `prepareLocalCapabilityAccountSecrets` cover local `model run`, `embedding create`, image `generate`/`edit`, image `describe`/`describe-many`, audio `transcribe`, video `generate`/download, and video `describe`. Their shared preparation retains the selected identity and validates before credential use. No command-specific predicates were added.

`capability` is an alias for the same registered command tree at `src/cli/capability-cli.ts:106-124`, as documented by `docs/cli/infer.md:9`; it reaches the same preparation owner.

Test consumers: `src/cli/capability-cli/local-account-secrets.test.ts:35,49` imports and calls the preparation helper for source-config provenance, and lines 18-20 mock the new auth-owner adapter for isolation. `src/cli/capability-cli.test.ts:336-338` mocks shared preparation for command-wiring coverage.

`assertAuthProfileStoreAgentOwner` has one production caller: shared local capability account preparation. The existing canonical assertion remains used by agent database schema, read-only access, writable open, admission, and maintenance. Model preparation also reaches that same assertion through persisted model-catalog reads.

Memory CLI uses its separate config-reference preparation in `extensions/memory-core/src/cli-runtime-common.ts`; adversarial finding F4 remains separate. Provider listings, web, and speech synthesis do not consume this helper.

Related open PRs #145188 and #145171 forward agent identity through media-understanding calls. They are separate from this saved-credential admission. Preserve the shared preparation call when reconciling landing order. Their branches and metadata were not changed.

## Invalidation

No owner verdict is cached. Every shared preparation call reads durable metadata, before the active-snapshot shortcut. Existing auth read-pool lifecycle and credential revision invalidation remain the owners. Credential mutation advances the revision; snapshot activation validates it; clearing the runtime clears linked snapshots. Database/root closure and process exit close pooled readers. No additional cache or lifecycle was introduced.

## Contention

No explicit transaction, lock, or queue is held across an await. The short metadata read uses the existing auth read connection and busy policy. Credential preparation retains its existing asynchronous lifecycle.

## Tests

The registered entry points `infer image generate`, `infer image describe`, `infer embedding create`, `infer audio transcribe`, `infer video generate`, and `infer video describe` each first succeed for their durable owner, then reject another selected identity without further credential egress, with both active and cleared secrets snapshots.

Deletion ledger: removed the helper-only “does not replace an already active secrets runtime snapshot” case because its no-directory-resolution assertion preserved the unsafe bypass. The registered-command cases now cover admission with an active snapshot. The helper source-config provenance case remains, with its new database dependency mocked to keep fixed paths isolated.

Moved side effects: none. Production grows by 25 net lines to connect explicit selected identity to the existing durable decision through the version-tolerant auth reader.

fix: expose persistent session spawning in Telegram (#145543)

## What Problem This Solves

Telegram users could not request persistent delegation through the model-visible sessions_spawn tool. With conversation bindings enabled, its schema omitted thread and limited mode to run, despite the documented support for binding the current conversation.

Related: #42986. Reworks the discovery fix in #145543 with credit to @nimarosa and @JackpotHan. The dispatch also referenced #142986, which concerns a separate documentation change and is not closed here.

## Why This Change Was Made

Explicit spawn discovery now reads the channel's declared placement and current-conversation binding support through one shared owner. Tool registration and runtime prompt capabilities consume that result. The existing child-only automatic placement check remains in the ACP command path, so /acp spawn keeps its existing default and explicit binding controls.

The tool description now explains that binding can use the current conversation or a new thread. There are no config keys, persistence changes, migrations, or protocol changes.

## User Impact

When Telegram binding and spawn policy permit it, the model sees thread and both run and session modes. Persistent spawns can use the current conversation, and subsequent messages reach the bound child. Disabled spawn policy still hides those options. Discord keeps its existing binding options.

## Evidence

Baseline: dda647045420956f7900180c5ca32d457dbc4973.
Runtime proof commit: b5c59888235c2bc7f3699c0c63ec18544de59462. The following commit only refreshes generated tool/prompt fixtures and their expected override list; production code and runtime proof inputs are unchanged.

- Real Gateway HTTP ingress: POST /v1/chat/completions with the documented x-openclaw-message-channel: telegram header. Complete outbound provider requests were captured with Telegram loaded. Baseline: thread absent, mode.enum=["run"]. Candidate: boolean thread, mode.enum=["run","session"].
- A Discord request retained its existing thread and run/session options. After reloading disabled spawn policy, a new Telegram request again exposed only run and omitted thread.
- Real Telegram Test Server user flow: a local deterministic provider requested sessions_spawn(thread=true, mode=session). The tool returned accepted; the child replied in the conversation. A second user message 12 seconds later reached the persistent child with its earlier task and reply context and received a visible reply. Four complete provider requests and the Telegram event timeline were retained. This proves routing and execution with controlled provider output, not autonomous model decision quality.
- A source-blind validator independently repeated the real Telegram flow and passed every contract clause. Its runner reported a process-stop error after recording; process/port checks and supported lease recovery completed cleanup.
- An earlier live setup attempt timed out resolving the bot username before sending any message. Its empty provider capture and failure were retained. Numeric chat selection resolved setup; the successful run confirmed resource cleanup.
- Registered-tool regression failed on the baseline for the missing session mode. Final registration/schema suites passed 144 tests; unchanged ACP helper tests passed 3 tests, and Telegram ACP command siblings passed 2 tests. Formatting, scoped lint, line-limit and assertion checks passed. Full type checks remain with CI.

fix(ui): recover Nostr profile requests with saved credentials (#138975)

## What Problem This Solves

Nostr profile Save and Import stop after the first rejected credential, although the configured Gateway token is still available. A paired loopback browser sends its device credential first; the profile HTTP route requires the configured shared credential.

This repair carries @zhangguiping-xydt’s credential-recovery work forward. It extracts the existing avatar/geolocation request loop into a shared Control UI request owner and uses it for Nostr profile operations. Each mutation advances only after 401, checks that the form and connection still own the operation, and retains one request deadline. Mutation 403 responses remain terminal. Gateway authentication is unchanged.

## Evidence

Base `c0f8bcf8e7f7ec540d5c11686c7444b4d71c55c8`: a real paired browser on an isolated loopback Gateway sent one PUT and one POST; both returned 401 and showed a failure. The same handlers returned 200 with the configured shared token: profile publication persisted, and import returned the relay profile. The relay and credentials are synthetic and local.

Candidate `b26b18b8a6ce83b186eac5302271e8919d62df04` (production matches the verified browser build): independent real-browser Save and Import each recover from 401 to 200 and show completion, including after reload. Replacing the saved Gateway secret through the normal UI with a wrong value leaves both actions visibly failed; restoring it restores both actions. The iMessage configuration editor saved a disabled test configuration and retained it after reconnect/reload; no real account or message was used.

The corrected page, supplemental HTTP adapter, and geolocation suites pass: 46 cases. Unchanged auth/avatar suites retain their passing evidence. The exact final two rendered recovery cases fail on baseline production and pass on candidate production. The original browser-build diff is preserved separately from the final source/test binding. Formatting, syntax lint, line/assertion ratchets, and unused-export checks pass. Full typechecks and CI run on GitHub. Sanitized browser captures, network evidence, and the independent acceptance report are retained for review.

An existing form issue remains outside this repair: empty optional profile fields can fail server validation; Save was verified with valid values. Exhausted credentials retain the existing visible error formatting issue.

## Consumers

- `resolveControlUiAuthCandidates` remains the credential normalization owner. Gateway startup, application configuration, roster/chat avatars, channel/plugin icon loaders, and the Nostr page keep their existing credential order.
- Cross-tree test consumer: `src/gateway/user-profiles-http.auth.test.ts:124-158` uses the UI candidate selector and resource context to load an avatar through real HTTP under token, password, and trusted-proxy auth, then checks the returned PNG type and exact image bytes. The trusted-proxy case exercises shared-password recovery after device-token rejection. This test is unchanged.
- Removed `resolveControlUiAuthHeader`: its only production consumer was Nostr ChannelsPage. The page now passes all candidates; the obsolete header assertion is removed. `resolveControlUiAuthToken` remains for browser panels, browser thumbnails, and chat attachments.
- `fetchWithControlUiAuth` is the shared request loop for Nostr Save/Import and the existing `fetchGatewayContextResource` adapter. Avatar/geolocation GET requests retain 401/403 recovery, origin checks, cookies, context cancellation, and exhaustion errors.
- Nostr operation callers are ChannelsPage and the focused operation tests. Each caller supplies candidates and operation freshness. No native app calls the Nostr HTTP operation helpers; native credential handoff still reaches the shared connection owner.
- Application config, protected roster avatars, and plugin-icon loaders have distinct existing request lifecycles and are unchanged. This change does not claim to replace every HTTP reader.
- Pipeline endpoint: actual browser PUT/POST requests reach the registered Nostr HTTP route; request headers and HTTP outcomes are captured with credentials removed from shared evidence.
- Related open PR #105781 changes import drafts and cancellation policy. This repair keeps current import persistence and does not copy that change. #138032 is the relevant merged avatar cleanup; #138199 is an unrelated dependency update.

## Invalidation

- Each new profile action reads the current device token and connection credentials; no winning-credential cache is added.
- Credential edits replace the Gateway client; disconnect, pairing/reconnect, channel-source replacement, form replacement, cancel, and document reload retire the old page operation. The page rechecks ownership before another request.
- Shared avatar/geolocation requests retain their existing context AbortSignal and cache-reset notifications when origin, base path, or credentials change.
- In-flight accepted writes retain existing semantics: discarding a stale result does not undo a server write. No new full-request cancellation contract is introduced.

## Contention

No new lock, queue, transaction, or shared write slot is held. Each operation has its own deadline and request sequence. The existing Nostr handler publication queue is unchanged.

## Tests

- Registered `openclaw-channels-page` actions (`channels-page.test.ts:199`): click Nostr → Edit Profile → Save/Import; verify 401 recovery, exhausted credentials, terminal 403. Exact final recovery cases are red on baseline production and green on the candidate.
- Rendered lifecycle table (`channels-page.test.ts:763`): start Save/Import by button; settle 200/401 after channel-source replacement or disconnect. Pending 401 also retires after enabled Import Cancel, same-account Cancel/Edit Profile replacement, subscribed credential/client replacement, and element unmount. Assert one request, no stale notice, and no post-response refresh; a reopened form retains its fresh draft. Cancel during Save remains disabled.
- Rendered deadline table (`channels-page.test.ts:845`): both Save/Import, with and without recovery. First rejection at 15 seconds starts the saved-credential request; the active request is not aborted at 29,999 ms, and the active request aborts at 30 seconds with the exact timeout notice and usable action button.
- Supplemental `nostr-profile-ops.test.ts` calls HTTP helpers directly for request shape, total/body deadline, successful and non-JSON responses. These remain adapter checks and are not counted as registered UI-action proof.
- Avatar/geolocation siblings: GET 401/403 recovery and credential-context invalidation.
- Existing WhatsApp channel editor test: rejected configuration remains visible without discarding the draft.
- Deletion ledger: retired the obsolete single-header assertion and `NostrTestPage` private-method seam. Rewrote source/disconnect/replacement/timeout cases through rendered controls; kept 200/401 stale-result and timeout behavior. The former private cross-account assertion is replaced by visible same-account fresh-draft preservation, not claimed as cross-account UI proof. Candidate/token assertions and supplemental adapter cases remain.
- No schema, configuration key, protocol, persistence format, Gateway auth, or upgrade migration change.

fix(sessions): recover omitted historical transcripts in Doctor (#120781)

* fix(sessions): stop doctor archiving live transcripts as orphans (#73471)

`openclaw doctor` treats a transcript as an orphan unless its path is the
CURRENT `sessionId` of some entry in `sessions.json`. That is not what a
session store holds, so the scan reports live history as unreferenced and
offers to archive it. Renamed files are then hard-deleted 30 days later by
`cleanupArchivedSessionTranscripts`.

Two independent causes:

1. `resolveSessionFilePath` can only rebuild `<sessionId>.jsonl` unless the
   entry carries `sessionFile`, and `sessionFile` is persisted for the live
   session only. Transcripts generated as `<iso-stamp>_<sessionId>.jsonl`
   therefore never resolve for any *previous* session in a compaction chain.
   Falls back to a name-based lookup via the existing
   `extractGeneratedTranscriptSessionId` helper, only when the canonical path
   is absent, so a brand-new session still gets the plain name.

2. The orphan scan reads `entry.sessionId` alone, ignoring
   `usageFamilySessionIds` (every prior id in a compaction chain),
   `compactionCheckpoints[].sessionId` and `systemPromptReport.sessionId`.
   Referenced ids are now collected from all four and matched against the
   session id parsed out of each file name.

Measured on an install with 84 primary transcripts: 58 reported orphans
before, 0 after — every one was a false positive.

Both tests fail on the unpatched build.

fix(audio): preserve complete voice-note transcription (#145391)

## Problem and fix

A 25-minute voice note can return a successful transcript containing only its first 20 minutes. The audio decoder introduced in #141836 stops at 1,200 seconds, and downstream consumers receive plain transcript text with no indication that audio was omitted.

Remove that decoder cutoff and its matching decoded-buffer cap. Decode the complete input into a private temporary file, then upload sequential 80 ms frames from a small reusable buffer. The existing operation deadline, cancellation, transport policy, transcript-size checks, and error handling remain in place. The file handle and temporary workspace close when the attempt finishes or fails. Existing input-size and request-timeout settings still apply.

This reverses the 20-minute conversion choice in #141836. The inspected introduction and discussion give no measured resource requirement for that duration. Temporary storage avoids retaining the whole decoded recording on the JavaScript heap. No configuration key, schema, migration, or protocol field is added.

## Consumers

- `extensions/deepgram/audio-flux.ts`: `decodeDeepgramFluxAudio` has one caller, `transcribeDeepgramFluxAudio`; `DEEPGRAM_FLUX_MAX_PCM_BYTES` is private and has no outside reader. The decoder now writes a file instead of returning a full PCM buffer. Its only caller owns the file and reads it sequentially.
- `extensions/deepgram/audio.ts:41,68` dispatches the existing `transcribeDeepgramAudio` callback to the streaming implementation. Its default HTTP path is unchanged.
- Voice-note registration: `extensions/deepgram/openclaw.plugin.json:20–22` declares the media-understanding provider contract; `index.ts:11` registers the provider whose `transcribeAudio` callback is assigned in `media-understanding-provider.ts:10`. `src/plugins/registry-registrars-providers.ts:277–281` writes that registration to `registry.mediaUnderstandingProviders`. `src/media-understanding/provider-registry.ts:33–46` reads prepared providers or resolves the `mediaUnderstandingProviders` capability and builds the provider map; its lookup at `:66–70` returns the selected provider.
- `extensions/deepgram/capability-catalog.ts:4–6` exposes realtime transcription only. It does not expose the voice-note callback changed by this PR.
- `src/media-understanding/runner.entries.ts:897–933` invokes the registered callback and consumes `result.text`. `src/media-understanding/runtime.ts:425–448` carries the result to `src/cli/capability-cli/audio.ts:39–60,79–88`, which delivers the existing CLI output.
- `src/media-understanding/audio-transcription-runner.ts:47–49` extracts the transcript string. `src/media-understanding/audio-preflight.ts:78` stores only `transcribed: true` on the matching attachment fact; it returns the transcript separately at `:88`. `extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-context.body.ts:307–320` reads that returned string and passes it to `src/plugin-sdk/media-understanding-runtime.ts:18–20` to frame the agent input. Telegram proof inspects the complete transcript at the final model-request boundary.
- The ordinary media-apply path also reads audio transcription outputs: `src/media-understanding/apply.ts:236–245` formats them into `ctx.Transcript` and, when there is no original user text, `ctx.CommandBody` and `ctx.RawBody`.
- `MEDIA_FFMPEG_MAX_AUDIO_DURATION_SECS` remains owned by `src/media/ffmpeg-limits.ts` and exported by `src/plugin-sdk/media-runtime.ts`. Its separate outbound-audio consumers in `extensions/discord/src/voice-message.ts`, `extensions/feishu/src/media.ts`, and `extensions/whatsapp/src/outbound-media-contract.ts` remain unchanged. Only this decoder stops consuming it.
- `docs/providers/deepgram.md` documents whole-file conversion and the remaining input/time limits. UI and native clients continue to consume ordinary message text; no new value shape reaches them.

## Contention

No shared lock, queue, transaction, or single-writer is held by the changed plugin code. Decoding, file handles, and sequential socket writes belong to one attempt. The real-decoder regression starts a second HTTP transcription after the long upload starts and verifies that it finishes before the long request is released.

## Invalidation

No shared cache or persisted derived value is added or changed. Each attempt creates its own temporary audio file and disposes it before returning. Reload and restart do not reuse converted audio.

## Tests

The latest rebase is head `c8d5800f76c250db0c4b1b9c642c57359d8c8cc8`, onto main `bca261d5583d12f73ed67f9f9df73089d68a0aca`. Range-diff confirms both contribution commits are unchanged. The following CLI and Telegram captures retain their tested head `f00b48c6`; they are reused because audio, registry, process, temporary-file and transport owners are unchanged. New adjacent branches apply to update requests and update canaries, which these fixtures do not enter. Fresh CI, merge-tree census and independent review assess the new head.

Earlier validation ran at head `f00b48c6940dde8bbe8cc1a522d0ae2032c817f3` and CI merge tree `0f5c7bb522dec992db8e4f96f0ffd35a864f58b3`. Those public CLI and Telegram runs confirmed complete audio delivery and the late marker through the changed registry and session owners. Earlier runtime captures remain pre-rebase evidence accepted by reviews at `3b4eec76a35b8cc7a2021e07f74b46744122a475` and `ca77dee9616e097c14062398aa36d39b169c44e0`; they are not relabeled as new-head runs. The original defect base remains `d30cf296be6fc137d1a6205180fb04a841c174e2`. Decoder and installed-release compatibility evidence is retained because those owners and contracts are unchanged.

- Production CLI, pinned base `d30cf296be6fc137d1a6205180fb04a841c174e2`: generated 1,500 seconds of real audio with spoken words at 21:00. The recording endpoint received 1,200 seconds / 38,400,000 bytes. The CLI exited 0 with `ok: true`, omitted the late words, and supplied no partial fact.
- Same CLI on the candidate: endpoint received all 1,500 seconds / 48,000,000 bytes, and the delivered transcript contained the late words. Exit 0. The before/after temporary-workspace census was empty.
- `audio-flux.live.test.ts`: `index.ts` registration → registered `transcribeAudio` → real ffmpeg → local protocol endpoint. Failed on the base with `prefix only` instead of `late marker`; passed after repair, with byte-for-byte coverage and the concurrent sibling check. This fixture requires ffmpeg and uses no external provider credential.
- `audio-flux.test.ts`: protocol, deadline, malformed-response, transcript-size, and network-policy cases now invoke the callback obtained from `index.ts` registration. The decoder fake writes its PCM output to the real output-file boundary. Together with unchanged `audio.test.ts` sibling cases: 18 passed. The real-decoder regression adds one passing test.
- Published `v2026.9.4` host: original plugin reproduced the cutoff. The candidate plugin, built through the repository package-runtime builder, returned the late words on that installed host while reusing its previous state directory. Both CLI runs exited 0; no migration was needed.
- Telegram Test Server: a real user driver sent the 25-minute voice note. The endpoint received all audio, and the recorded model request contained the late words in its audio transcript. The bot replied, the runner completed, its scratch state was removed, and its listeners closed. Inference was deterministic; this proves transcript delivery, not speech-recognition quality or model judgment.
- Focused formatting and lint passed. Full CI, merge-tree structural checks, and exact-head landing review are required before merge.

### Deletion ledger and moved responsibilities

No test was deleted. The protocol-case assertion requiring `-t 1200` and a 38,400,000-byte buffer was removed because it enshrined the defect. Full-audio coverage moves to the registered-callback real-decoder regression. Existing request, transcript, policy, and deadline assertions remain; the deadline case now awaits asynchronous cleanup after advancing the original deadline.

Decoded-audio storage moves from the full stdout buffer to the existing temporary-workspace owner; a scoped file handle owns reads. The process helper still owns decoder cancellation and timeout, and the existing socket owner still owns connection cleanup. No parallel implementation or compatibility alias remains.

fix(signal): repair unconfigured account keys in doctor (#138982)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes configured Signal accounts such as `Work Phone` being listed as `work-phone` but skipped as unconfigured.

## Why This Change Was Made

Signal Doctor moves unambiguous account keys onto the same normalized IDs used by account listing. Runtime readers keep their existing lookup contract. Entire account entries survive the move; collisions remain unchanged and receive rename guidance. Aliases that already inherit a configured account or default transport remain unchanged with guidance, so Doctor cannot switch a working route. Signal keeps root account settings when an account map already exists, using the existing plugin promotion declaration. Shared setup defaults and first-account setup remain unchanged.

## User Impact

Run `openclaw doctor --fix`, then restart the Gateway to activate the repaired account. Collisions require an explicit rename.

Credit: @marmar9615-cloud for the original report and Doctor repair approach. This revision narrows #138982 to account-key repair. No linked issue was present on the original PR.

## Consumers

The reinterpreted value is a key in `channels.signal.accounts`: a repairable authored key becomes the canonical ID already returned by listing. Complete account entries move together. Entry fields, `defaultAccount`, route IDs, and status/protocol fields are not renamed. This census covers that stored-key change, not only removed symbols.

- Repair dispatch: `extensions/signal/config-doctor-api.ts:64` and `extensions/signal/src/doctor.ts:7` feed `src/commands/doctor/shared/channel-legacy-config-migrate.ts:103`, `legacy-config-core-migrate.ts:150` in the same directory, and `src/commands/doctor-config-flow.ts:425` and `:546`. The transform returns a candidate; `src/commands/doctor/finalize-config-flow.ts:20` owns whether Doctor persists it, using existing writes and backups.
- Listing and runtime resolution: `extensions/signal/src/accounts.ts:49` and `src/channels/plugins/account-helpers.ts:58` normalize listed/requested IDs; account/default resolution and derived settings continue through `extensions/signal/src/accounts.ts:237` and `:282`. Signal's `resolveSignalAccountConfig` at `accounts.ts:58` still calls `src/config/channel-account-config.ts:60` without the optional normalized-key lookup. Its runtime lookup remains exact-key first, then case-insensitive, through `src/routing/account-lookup.ts:15`; this PR adds no runtime alias fallback.
- Existing normalized selectors remain distinct: `resolveNormalizedAccountEntry` in `src/routing/account-lookup.ts:27` supports generic readers, including `src/channels/plugins/read-only.ts:202`; `extensions/signal/src/config-compat.ts:330` uses its existing first-normalized-key selector for transport migration; `src/channels/plugins/setup-helpers.ts:318` uses its existing `resolveExistingAccountKey` for setup writes. This PR neither introduces nor replaces those selectors.
- Setup promotion: `src/channels/plugins/setup-contract.ts:343` forwards the existing declaration, `setup-promotion-helpers.ts:136` reads it, and `setup-helpers.ts:369` in that directory plus `src/commands/doctor/shared/legacy-config-core-normalizers.ts:157` consume the decision. `extensions/signal/src/setup-core.ts:362` retains setup writes and restored-default handling; its `namedAccountPromotionKeys` declaration keeps inherited root settings when account entries already exist. Shared defaults and first-account promotion stay unchanged.
- Other Signal config writers: `extensions/signal/src/setup-transport.ts:111` and `:319` select/write account transport; `extensions/signal/src/shared.ts:32` exposes enable/delete/default-target operations through `src/channels/plugins/config-helpers.ts:74`. These continue to operate on the repaired stored map through their existing contracts.
- Schema and legacy transport: `extensions/signal/src/config-schema.ts:146` iterates account entries and selects the default account. `extensions/signal/src/config-compat.ts:378` and `:475` retain transport cleanup writes after the normalized selection cited above. Complete entries survive key repair before these existing streaming/transport repairs run.
- Shared policy/config readers: `src/config/group-policy.ts:74`, `src/config/context-visibility.ts:53`, `src/config/markdown-tables.ts:53`, `src/auto-reply/chunk.ts:45` and `:87`, and `src/auto-reply/reply/block-streaming.ts:58` consume account settings from the repaired map.
- Shared enablement, authorization, media, and repair readers: `src/channels/account-config-enabled.ts:11`, `src/channels/plugins/config-write-policy-shared.ts:70` and `:85`, `src/auto-reply/command-auth.ts:445`, `src/media/configured-max-bytes.ts:35`, and `src/commands/doctor/shared/legacy-config-binding-repair.ts:96` retain their existing account-selection contracts.
- Signal setup and inbound runtime consumers (paths under `extensions/signal/`): `src/setup-surface.ts:34`, `src/monitor.ts:307` and `:395`, and `src/monitor/event-handler.ts:272` obtain the complete repaired entry through the unchanged resolver.
- Signal outbound and action consumers (paths under `extensions/signal/`): `src/send.ts:115` and `:294`, `src/send-reactions.ts:37`, `src/message-actions.ts:62` and `:100`, `src/reaction-level.ts:26`, and `src/aliases.ts:40` consume the same resolved settings.
- Signal approval and exported runtime consumers (paths under `extensions/signal/`): `src/approval-auth.ts:24`, `src/approval-native.ts:29` and `:39`, and `src/approval-handler.runtime.ts:125` consume resolved account settings. `src/rpc-context.ts:5` consumes the resolved account type; `api.ts` and `runtime-api.ts` retain their existing exports.
- Pipeline endpoint: `src/gateway/server-channels.ts:791`, `:824`, `:922`, and `:978` resolve/admit accounts; `extensions/signal/src/channel.ts:590` starts the provider at its endpoint; `src/gateway/server-methods/channels.ts:493` composes account status. Retained startup logs and real `channels.status` responses verify that the repaired entry reaches these endpoints.
- UI/native status consumers: `ui/src/pages/channels/view.ts:181` and `ui/src/pages/channels/view.detail.ts:57` and `:74` consume the status rows; `apps/android/app/src/main/java/ai/openclaw/app/NodeRuntime.kt:9423` consumes account rows; `apps/shared/OpenClawKit/Sources/OpenClawProtocol/GatewayModels.swift:3570` and `:3615` retain `channelAccounts`. These clients do not reinterpret stored account keys, and no client repair or protocol change is added.
- Documentation consumers: `docs/channels/signal.md:84`, `:267`, `:305`, `:315`, `:351`, and `:491`; `docs/gateway/config-channels/personal-messaging.md:150`; and the existing promotion declaration documentation at `docs/plugins/sdk-setup.md:440`. The Signal page instructs operators to run Doctor and restart.
- No exports, schema keys, protocol fields, or CLI options are removed. Other channels are untouched. Collision groups retain their authored order and entries; the transform does not change existing runtime selection within a collision.

## Invalidation

- **Observed:** Doctor persisted the repaired config through its existing write owner, then a Gateway restart read the repaired map and started the account at its authored endpoint. The verified operator sequence remains `openclaw doctor --fix`, then restart the Gateway.
- **Source evidence only:** Signal registers `channels.signal` in `reload.configPrefixes` at `extensions/signal/src/shared.ts:114`. Core consumes plugin reload prefixes for channel restart planning at `src/gateway/config-reload-plan.ts:302` and `:549`. This supports a source-inferred live-reload path; live reload after a Doctor write was **not exercised** in the retained proof.
- No new cache is introduced. The existing normalized-ID cache in `src/routing/account-id.ts:38` is keyed by the input string and needs no config invalidation. Account maps, defaults, and merged settings are recomputed from config; running monitors hold a config snapshot that the verified restart refreshes. Repeated repair leaves the stored account map unchanged.

## Contention

No locks, queues or transactions are held by the pure key transform. Existing Doctor config persistence owns its write protection.

## Tests

117 focused Signal tests, 23 routing tests, and 58 startup config/state corpus tests passed. The new regression cases fail against the original Doctor contracts and catch the first candidate’s warning and route failures. Source review is clear. Fresh independent Gateway controls passed: canonical settings, other-channel isolation, collision guidance in preview and repair, inherited-route preservation, and stable second repairs. Previous-release proof passed: the source-built `v2026.9.4` CLI wrote the fixture, its Gateway reproduced the defect, and this candidate booted the saved state. Doctor preview preserved the authored key and explained the move; repair made the account start at its authored endpoint. A second repair left the complete Signal config unchanged.

The following are registered plugin-contract tests, not full Doctor command tests. `extensions/signal/doctor-contract-api.ts:1` exports the compatibility contract registered by `doctorContract.configRepair` in `extensions/signal/openclaw.plugin.json:6`; the live plugin attaches `signalDoctor` at `extensions/signal/src/shared.ts:119`. Separate retained CLI/Gateway runs cover the complete command, persistence, promotion ordering, and startup flow.

| New test in `extensions/signal/doctor-contract-api.test.ts` | Registered entry point exercised | Last assertion boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Complete named account and other channel, line 17 | Signal Doctor `normalizeCompatibilityConfig` | Stored map, actual `resolveSignalAccount`, unchanged other channel, second normalization |
| Inherited account: `Work Phone`, `Default.`, and `!!!`, line 45 | Signal Doctor `normalizeCompatibilityConfig` and registered `signalDoctor.cleanStaleConfig`; real setup promotion with the Signal adapter runs first | Actual resolver retains the root number; stored entries remain unchanged; cleanup warning |
| Collision: `Work.Phone`, `work-phone`, and `WORK-PHONE`, line 70 | Signal Doctor `normalizeCompatibilityConfig` and registered `signalDoctor.cleanStaleConfig` | Both entries remain, no repair changes, collision guidance |
| Active default transport plus independent named repair, line 87 | Signal Doctor `normalizeCompatibilityConfig` | Resulting map and actual default account's endpoint and number |

No baseline tests are deleted or rewritten. Preparation replaced newly added preview-hook assertions from the rejected candidate with cleanup-hook assertions used by both Doctor modes. The original contributor branch's shared setup implementation and tests are excluded; the existing Signal-specific declaration preserves its routes. The 117/23/58 passing logs use the execution ledger and unchanged inputs for historical attribution; they do not each embed a final-head SHA. No unchanged test input was rerun solely to restamp it.

## Evidence

Baseline `f96c900b1d42`: the real isolated Gateway listed `work-phone` with `configured: false`, `running: false`, and `stateReason: not configured`.

Candidate `f50b80a3dc75`: `doctor --fix --non-interactive` persisted `work-phone`; the same `gateway call channels.status --params '{"channel":"signal","probe":false}' --json` reported `configured: true`, `running: true`, and a start time. The startup log selected the authored external-native endpoint. Both CLI requests and Doctor exited 0. The unused loopback endpoint refuses connections as expected; daemon health and delivery are not claimed.

No schemas, config keys or protocol fields change. The key transform adds no persistence owner; existing Doctor writes and backups remain authoritative.
